body.statement: Let \(p_{ij}=q_0\in(q,1-q)\), \(n/m\to c_0\in(0,\infty)\), and \(r=\mu=K=1\). If \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{n\log n}\), then \(b_{nm}\asymp1\), and bounded nonzero common arm means give \(\sqrt n\lVert EV/\sigma_1(M)\rVert_\infty=\Omega_P(1)\). If \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{nm}\), then \(b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt{\log n/n}\), the independent full-matrix maximum-row scale. Also \(Z^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}+D^{\mathrm B}+R^{\mathrm B}\), with \(D^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=-(\widehat p_i-q_0)[\mu^1_{ij}/q_0+\mu^0_{ij}/(1-q_0)]\); this is generally first order, and it vanishes only when the displayed derivative loading is zero.
body.justification: This pins down the signal regimes and shows why empirical row normalization has its own first-order tangent.
body.gap: Mehrotra et al.'s public Algorithm 1 gives the independent-assignment empirical-row-scaling benchmark for separate arm fits; the signed recorded-score decomposition here isolates the denominator tangent relevant to the new blind procedure.
body.consumer: Analysts can distinguish a fixed known denominator from a random row-total normalization.
